proposed_facts.reason: Singleton declarations establish the logical fields. The update tests the enable bit, whereas cleanup clears it unconditionally; the replacement avoids claiming compiled layout.

The canonical branches skip timer -1, decrement positive timers without same-visit spawning, and otherwise attempt resolution. Bounds, dispatch, occupancy, reciprocal indices and cyclic termination agree with the proposal, including its invalid-index and unintended-negative-state qualifications.
Reserved entries are conditionally writable storage. Traversal terminates by cyclic index rather than a sentinel, making ConfigureReservedEntry meaningfully more accurate.

The source signature and stores establish argument order and s16 narrowing. Ground separately resolves the marker and forwards the payload to the Coin constructor, which retains it and requests its trophy-display model.
The complete registration body conditionally stores marker, payload and NULL occupancy without changing timers, validating arguments or constructing an item.

A narrowed marker of -1 leaves the entry marker-unused despite other stores. Ground explicitly returns -1 on selection failure, and Shrine Route forwards the result unchecked. The proposed state distinction is necessary.

Only registry servicing tests the enable bit. Registration and lifecycle mutations are ungated; cleanup disables first, and item destruction invokes a destroyed callback that can forward to the generator handler.

Cleanup disables updates and sweeps eligible global item kinds without freeing the registry or removing its manager. Kinoko Route subsequently re-enables updates, supporting the reversible disable-and-cleanup name.

contradictions.reason: Accept the .bss layout deferral: source declarations establish logical singleton fields, not compiled section attribution or extent. The enable-purpose contradiction is resolved by proposal 0. Supported unchanged research is retained without equivalent rewrites.

Accept deferral of the three .data claims: the failure diagnostic is visible, but section membership, exclusivity, extent and padding are not established. Including NUL, the filename has 17 bytes and the format has 26 bytes; the legacy counts are not affirmed.

Accept deferral of the three .sdata claims. The allocation assertion is supported, but its expression's section association, section size and padding require compiled evidence. The restored allocation range uses the correct pinned revision.
Accept deferral of .sdata2 literal membership, pool-size, ordering and section-purpose claims. Source establishes zero, epsilon and half-bound uses, not emitted section bytes.

Accept explicit deferral, not retention, of the conflated .sdata2 gameplay fact and link. Segment intersections drive independent callbacks; registry candidates use stage markers. Corneria supplies and updates separate segment configurations. Compiled section attribution remains unverified.

The zero-only timer explanation is superseded correctly by proposal 1. Decrement-to-zero does not spawn on that visit; other negative values except -1 reach resolution without being established as intended states.

Proposals 2–5 resolve all five reserved-entry contradictions: the tail is usable storage rather than a traversal sentinel, arguments have independently traced payload/marker roles, and field mutation does not guarantee activation. Unchecked -1 forwarding is a real exceptional path.

Proposal 6 resolves the global-freeze contradiction: disabled update invocations preserve state, but lifecycle callbacks and registration can still mutate it. Registry lifetime must extend through cleanup's destruction callbacks.
Proposal 7 resolves the final-teardown implication of Shutdown. The routine performs reversible disablement and item cleanup, and the route controller later enables the same facility.
